q1.title: Is tc1 actually closed?
q1.imperative: Answer from evidence I produced myself.
q1.finding: TC1 IS CLOSED. I rebuilt my own g1 adversarial case from scratch (scratchpad/attack_g1b.py): real git init + real git worktree add, both trees holding a valid checklist at .agent-work/shared/spine.json, command carrying NO cd and NO --worktree, hook run in a FRESH SUBPROCESS, nothing monkeypatched. I seeded the store with {"pre-existing": {}} FIRST so 'byte-unchanged' is a real comparison and not empty-vs-empty. Result: BYTE-UNCHANGED = True, store keys = ['pre-existing'], no sidA key. Under g1 this same case bound the main checkout's copy with path_source 'payload_cwd'. Also confirmed the two supporting shapes: two disagreeing rung-4 worktree roots bind nothing, and a single validating rung-4 root still binds with path_source 'git_worktree'.

q2.title: Did the guard overshoot into a regression?
q2.imperative: Answer from evidence I produced myself.
q2.finding: NO REGRESSION REACHES A LIVE SHAPE. I TESTED THE COMMANDER'S READING RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT (scratchpad/reach_g1b.py, read-only over the REAL trees). Method: for every registered worktree, intersect the relative paths that hold a VALIDATING checklist in the main checkout with those in that worktree, keep only pairs that are DIFFERENT files - those are exactly the paths a relative --file claim now silences. Result: 2693 colliding relative paths across all worktrees, of which LIVE (untracked in main, i.e. a real in-flight spine) = ZERO. Every collision is a tracked, archived work area that will never be claimed again (epic-298 harvest/pre/post runs, explore-* cycles, scout-*). Checked the two live spines by name: .agent-work/epic-418/spine.json is UNTRACKED and present ONLY in the main checkout ('git ls-files --error-unmatch' errors; a per-tree existence sweep finds it only in C:/Programs/constellation-skills), and .agent-work/issue-440-binding-cwd/execute.json exists ONLY in the worktree - so neither the Admiral's claim nor this Commander's claim can be silenced. Constructed both regression shapes directly too: a main-checkout agent whose worktree holds NO checklist at that path still binds the correct main path with path_source 'payload_cwd'; the true silencing shape (both trees hold one) binds nothing, which is the deliberate trade. Told-truth rungs are NOT silenced under ambiguity - verified all three against a real two-tree collision: cd_target, worktree_opt and absolute --file each still bound the worktree spine outright. The Commander's reading holds.

q3.title: The 4 deletions - stricter or relaxed?
q3.imperative: Answer from evidence I produced myself.
q3.finding: STRENGTHENED, not relaxed - and the count is exactly right this time. 'git diff --numstat 9d44aa6' gives tests/test_spine_rail.py = 156 insertions, 4 DELETIONS, and enumerating every '-' line confirms all 4 sit in test_git_probe_does_not_run_when_an_earlier_rung_answers: 2 docstring lines (replaced by a 9-line one) and 2 assertions. Neither assertion was loosened in FORM - both were and remain exact list-equality, no '>=', no len() bound, no deletion. 'assert calls == []' -> 'assert calls == [str(proj)]' pins BOTH an exact call count of one AND the exact argument, which is strictly more than the old assertion said about a call that occurs. The second, 'assert calls == []' -> 'assert calls == [str(proj)]  # unchanged -- rung 0 added no probe of its own', still proves rung 0 short-circuits, by asserting the list did NOT grow. I verified INDEPENDENTLY that the new assertions describe reality rather than being fitted to it: my own subprocess.run spy (q3_tail.py) shows the guessed-rung claim now spawns exactly one ['git','worktree','list','--porcelain'] and the absolute --file claim adds none. So the assertions track a real, deliberate, documented behaviour change. SEE q4 for the finding this behaviour change carries.

q4.title: Never raises, probe bounded and off the told-truth path
q4.imperative: Answer from evidence I produced myself.
q4.finding: Never raises; probe still bounded; off the TOLD-TRUTH path but NO LONGER off the guessed path. Re-ran my 23 hostile payload shapes from the g1 review unchanged -> 23 rows, 0 failures, all returned {} with no raise. GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS still 2.0; non-repo dir -> [] in 0.029s; nonexistent cwd -> [] in 0.001s; TimeoutExpired -> [], OSError -> [], MemoryError -> []. FINDING (minor, honest, already documented by the implementer): the g1 close criterion 'the git probe is off the common path' NO LONGER HOLDS in its g1 form. My subprocess spy shows a plain rung-3 claim now spawns one 'git worktree list --porcelain' where g1 spawned none - unavoidable, since a guess cannot be known unambiguous without consulting the later guesses. Told-truth rungs still never probe (rung 0 added no call even with two trees disagreeing). Cost is bounded and small: it fires only on an engine claim/release, roughly twice per run rather than once per tool call, capped at 2.0s, and degrades to [] on any failure. The module docstring and the revised test docstring both state this plainly rather than hiding it. SECOND FINDING (minor): the test is now NAMED test_git_probe_does_not_run_when_an_earlier_rung_answers but asserts the probe DOES run when an earlier GUESSED rung answers. The docstring explains; the name contradicts the assertion and should be renamed before it misleads a future reader.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. tc1 is closed, verified by rebuilding my own g1 adversarial case on a real git worktree in a fresh subprocess with a pre-seeded store: BYTE-UNCHANGED True, nothing bound, where g1 bound the main checkout. The guard did NOT overshoot into a live regression - I tested the Commander's reading rather than accepting it, sweeping every registered worktree against the main checkout: 2693 colliding relative paths, ZERO of them live/untracked; both live spines (.agent-work/epic-418/spine.json, .agent-work/issue-440-binding-cwd/execute.json) exist in exactly one tree each and cannot be silenced. Told-truth rungs all still win outright under a real two-tree collision. The 4 deletions are strengthening: all in one test, 2 docstring lines plus 2 assertions rewritten from 'calls == []' to 'calls == [str(proj)]' - still exact equality, now pinning both count and argument, and I confirmed by independent subprocess spy that they describe real behaviour. Never raises over 23 hostile shapes; probe bounded at 2.0s with TimeoutExpired/OSError/MemoryError all handled. GREEN 176 passed exit 0; RED 4 failed against 9d44aa6 for the right reason. Two minor findings, neither blocking: the git probe is no longer off the GUESSED-rung path (one bounded git call per engine claim/release, honestly documented), and the revised test's name now contradicts its assertion. Tree restored byte-identically; nothing committed.

triage_candidates.statement: Rename test_git_probe_does_not_run_when_an_earlier_rung_answers - since g1b it asserts the probe DOES run when an earlier GUESSED rung answers, so the name contradicts its own assertion. Cheap rename, no behaviour change.

The g1b guard's silencing reach is a function of which checklists are TRACKED under .agent-work/. Today zero live spines collide, but that is a property of current repo content, not an invariant - a future run whose work-id matches a tracked archived work area would bind nothing silently, with no signal. Consider either a diagnostic breadcrumb when the guard refuses, or excluding .agent-work/archive/ from what looks_like_checklist will accept as a candidate.
